order: Build the alias layer and the roster kill switch before any rename. In the aliases file, declare every retired name's role and rung pair, the legacy identity it keeps while the old roster is installed, and its ledger deprecation line. Have the seat resolver evaluate the roster flag per order, so legacy returns the installed legacy agent unchanged while new goes through the casting tables and the degradation machine, with the declarative default at legacy as the kill-switch home position, so rollback is a flag flip with no reload. Load the map under the same fail-closed discipline the other tables get, so an unknown role, a rung the named role does not have, a missing legacy identity, or a bad roster default must each refuse construction. Prove it, with old-name orders dispatching under both flag values, the flip demonstrated mid-session on one instance, every retired-name resolution emitting its deprecation line, and a tampered map failing the load closed.
claims: The aliases map declares all 16 retired names with role, rung, identity and deprecation line. The resolver reads the flag per order, defaulting to legacy, so rollback is a flag flip. Old-name orders dispatch under both flags, flipped mid-session. It loads fail-closed on an unknown role, a rung the named role does not have, a missing identity or bad default; section 12 hands a tampered map whose alias names a rung its role lacks and asserts the refusal. Suite green, 93 passed.
